analysis: Examined the supplied excerpts of MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift. The base units (lines 1436-2081) cover the native media path, makeEventStream forwarding, lease handoff, the terminal-drain logic and the tokenizer utilities. The head unit covers lines 1-518: the struct, initializers, acquire flow and the start of prepareCompletion. The changed ranges (head 1024-1035, 1078, 1108-1173) are visible only in the truncated patch excerpt, not in numbered head text. The changes visible there add GenerationLoopExitThinkingPolicy.resolve and pass exitThinking into GenerationLoopGuardPolicy.resolve. A new local stopStringScope is hoisted out of the bridge-submit call. The exit-thinking policy is disabled unless engineV2Bridge reports servesDistributedPair == false. Because `await engineV2Bridge?.servesDistributedPair != false` is true for a nil bridge, a missing bridge also disables the feature, so it fails closed. No change was seen to the coordinator-sealed request handling, cache scope (cacheScope/cacheSalt plumbing, T-041), decryption, or authorization/attestation boundaries. The stop-string scope is computed from the same inputs as before. Plaintext-exposure paths (T-008) and release/cancel semantics in makeEventStream are unchanged in the base text. No concrete security regression was found. Remaining uncertainty: the patch from head line ~1108 to 1173 is truncated. The implementations of GenerationLoopExitThinkingPolicy and GenerationLoopGuardPolicy, and any injected token or logit-processing behavior, are not visible. A deeper review should confirm that exit-thinking injection cannot alter prefix-cache keys, billing and usage accounting, or logprob behavior, and cannot leak withheld reasoning (withholdReasoning) to the consumer.
